metaDescription: Six 25 pint dehumidifiers compared on pump drainage, cold-room limits, Wi-Fi control and efficiency ratings, with a firm pick for each kind of basement.
expertTake: The Levoit 25 pint is the pick for most basements because it combines an Energy Star Most Efficient rating with four drain methods, including a removable pump that lifts water up to 3 meters. The Hisense is the value pick for a cool room, with a stated low-temperature limit of 38 F. Skip the whole 25 pint class if your basement walls sweat in summer; a larger machine will serve you better.
introParagraphs: A dehumidifier in this size band is the sweet spot for a typical finished basement, a large bedroom or a laundry level. It is strong enough to hold humidity steady, small enough to move, and cheap enough to run for months at a stretch.

This guide explains how the daily rating is measured, why drainage and cold-room behavior matter more than the headline number, and how smart features and efficiency labels change ownership. Use the picks above as a shortlist, then read the reviews to find the fit for your space.

products.name: Levoit 25 Pint Dehumidifier DOE Energy Star Most Efficient with Pump
products.description:
Levoit gives you the cleanest set of numbers in the group. The listing separates a DOE rating of 25 pints from a maximum rating of 84 pints, so you can see how much of the bigger figure is marketing. It also carries the Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 label, which means the EPA picked it from the efficient end of the field.

The feature that sets it apart is drainage. There are four ways to remove water: gravity drain, garden hose, a removable pump and the tank itself, and the pump lifts water up to 3 meters. That solves the common basement problem where the drain is above the floor. Compared with the GE and Whirlpool, which rely on a gravity hose or bucket, the Levoit is the only unit here that can send water uphill without extra equipment.

Ownership is unusual because the pump is washable and removable, so a clog is something you clean rather than a reason to replace the unit. Rinse the filter regularly and check the pump hose once a season. The cost of this feature set is a bulkier body than a plain bucket unit.
products.bestFor: A basement where the drain sits above the floor or you want fully hands-free operation.
pros: DOE rating clearly separated from the max figure
Washable removable pump lifts water up to 3 m
Four drainage methods cover any layout
cons: More bulk than a basic bucket unit
More parts to clean than a simple design

products.name: LG PuriCare 25 Pint Smart Dehumidifier Wi-Fi Energy Star
products.description:
LG's PuriCare model is the connected pick. The ThinQ app adjusts settings, tracks performance and pushes maintenance alerts, which means a full bucket or a clogged filter becomes a message on your phone. It also carries an Energy Star certificate and is aimed at basements, laundry rooms and large rooms.

The usual question with an app-driven machine is what happens when the app ends. LG is a large appliance maker with a long app record, which is a better bet than a marketplace brand. Compared with the Levoit, the LG has fewer drainage routes in its listing and no stated pump, so it fits a basement with a floor drain better than one with a high drain.

Expect to spend a little time pairing the unit with your Wi-Fi, and expect the filter alert to be the most useful part. A strong signal in the basement helps, because the alerts only matter if they reach you. In day to day use the first thing most people notice is the filter alert, because lint builds fastest in a laundry setting. If your Wi-Fi drops often, set the humidity target on the unit itself so it keeps running regardless.
products.bestFor: People who want filter and status alerts on a phone for a basement unit.
pros: ThinQ app shows status and maintenance alerts
Large appliance brand with an established app
Aimed at laundry rooms and basements
cons: Fewer drainage routes than the Levoit
App features need a stable Wi-Fi signal

products.name: Hisense 25 Pint Compact Portable Dehumidifier 1,500 Sq Ft
products.description:
Hisense states a low-temperature limit of 38 F, which is rare in this class and the reason it earns the cool-room badge. A basement that drops in winter pushes a normal compressor unit into defrost, and a stated limit tells you the manufacturer designed for it. Controls are deliberately simple, with a continuous mode that you start by pressing the minus button until 'CO' appears.

The tradeoff is that the feature list is plain. You do not get an app, a pump or a color indicator, and the listing frames it as manual controls anyone can use. Set against the LG, the Hisense is the reliable but unflashy choice, and against the Levoit it gives up drainage options for a lower buying commitment.

It has the usual filter, bucket and coil care. A lower limit does not mean full output when cold, so expect reduced water removal in a 40 F space even though the unit keeps running. One practical point is that a stated limit is not a promise of full output: at 40 F the coil spends much of its time defrosting, so water removal may be only a fraction of the label. It is still better than a unit that quits.
products.bestFor: An unheated basement or garage space where cold-room operation matters more than apps.
pros: Continuous mode with one button hold
cons: Output still falls in genuinely cold air

products.name: GE 25 Pint Small Dehumidifier Smart Dry 1,500 Sq Ft
products.description:
GE's Smart Dry changes fan speed according to room humidity, so the machine slows down as the air gets drier instead of running flat out. This reduces noise and avoids over-drying, which matters in a bedroom where a constant roar would be unwelcome. The listing places it for a bedroom, bathroom or basement and includes a built-in hose connection.

The small print is that the drain hose is not included, so you will need to buy one if you want continuous drain. That is a small cost, but worth knowing. Against the Whirlpool, which also carries a familiar name, the GE emphasizes fan logic while the Whirlpool stresses carry features.

The filter and bucket need the same care as other units. GE's reputation for service is a useful backup if a part fails after the warranty. The Smart Dry logic also means it can sound noticeably quieter in the late stages of a drying cycle than at the start. That is where its comparison with a fixed-speed unit becomes obvious.
products.bestFor: A bedroom or bathroom unit that should slow down as the air dries.
pros: Smart Dry adjusts fan speed to humidity

products.name: Whirlpool 25 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier with Casters
products.description:
Whirlpool bundles casters and top carry handles so you can move it from room to room with little effort. That matters in a house where one unit serves the laundry, then a bedroom, then a basement. It is Energy Star certified, with electronic controls and an adjustable humidistat.

Beyond that, the listing offers few specifics. Compared with the Levoit it lacks pump or multi-drain features, and compared with the LG it lacks an app. The trade is a clean, familiar unit that does one job without extras. For many homes that is enough.

A unit you move often needs careful hose and bucket handling. Empty the bucket before rolling it, and keep the casters clear of lint so they do not scratch a finished floor. If you carry it up and down stairs, use the top handles and empty the tank first, since a full bucket shifts weight and strains the casing. Check that the electrical cord reaches without an extension.
products.bestFor: A household that moves one dehumidifier between rooms through the year.
pros: Casters and top handles ease moving

products.name: hOmeLabs 25 Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier 3,500 Sq Ft
products.description:
hOmeLabs names its rating conditions: 25 pints per day at 80 F and 60 percent humidity, with a maximum of 64 pints at 95 F and 90 percent. That is honest, but note that the 25 pint figure uses the older, easier 80 F test, so it is not directly comparable with the Levoit's DOE rating. Treat it as a smaller machine than its label looks next to a modern DOE number.

The 3,500 sq ft coverage claim is the biggest on paper, and it follows the same optimistic logic as other oversized claims. The better reason to buy is the Wi-Fi app at a modest cost. Against the LG, the hOmeLabs offers a similar connected experience in a less established brand.

Wash the filter often, since the compact body has little spare airflow. Check that the app keeps working after firmware changes, and keep the manual humidistat as the backup. Because the headline conditions differ, do not compare its 25 pints directly with the Levoit; mentally subtract a third for a fair match. A hygrometer in the room tells you whether it keeps up.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want an app-connected unit with disclosed rating conditions.
pros: Large coverage figure for open spaces
cons: 25 pints uses the older easier test

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Levoit lists a DOE 25 pints and a separate 84 pint maximum. The hOmeLabs states 25 pints at 80 F, an older and easier test, so it is a smaller machine than the label suggests. Compare only like with like, and remember that a modern DOE 25 equals roughly 35 on the pre-2019 scale.

A gravity drain needs the unit above the drain. The Levoit's removable pump lifts water up to 3 meters, which solves a high drain or a walk-up basement. If your drain is at floor level a gravity hose from the GE or Whirlpool is enough. Pumps also tolerate a long horizontal run, but a vertical lift near the limit reduces flow, so plan the shortest practical route.

Below about 65 F a compressor coil frosts and output drops. The Hisense states operation down to 38 F, and a limit on the spec sheet is more useful than a bare 'works in cold rooms'. Expect less water removal in an unheated space whatever the label says. Garages and crawl spaces swing even colder than basements, so measure the winter low with a cheap thermometer before choosing.

A unit running 12 hours a day costs more over a season than its purchase premium. The Levoit's Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 mark and the LG and Whirlpool Energy Star marks are checkable on the EPA site. An unlabeled efficient claim is not a substitute. Running cost scales with hours, so a damp house that needs 14 hours a day feels the difference far more than a dry one.

The LG ThinQ app sends maintenance alerts, which is useful for an unattended unit. A plain panel like the Hisense never breaks when a router changes. Prefer a smart unit only if the app exists from a manufacturer with a track record. Ask whether the app also controls the unit offline, and whether firmware updates are still being released two years after launch.

Square feet follow the pint number loosely. The hOmeLabs claims 3,500 sq ft and the GE and Hisense claim 1,500 for the same 25 pints. Use the lower figure and add one size step for a wet space. Ceiling height matters too, because the listing assumes a standard eight foot room.

specDecoder.meaning: Water removed per day at 65 F and 60 percent humidity. It is the strictest common rating. Multiply a DOE figure by about 1.4 to compare it with a pre-2019 label.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Levoit cites DOE while the hOmeLabs uses 80 F.

specDecoder.meaning: The best-case figure at about 95 F and 90 percent humidity. Real rooms rarely get there.
specDecoder.watchFor: Levoit's 84 pints and hOmeLabs' 64 pints describe hot, saturated air.

specDecoder.meaning: The lowest room temperature in which the unit keeps running. Output still falls. Defrost cycles lower the daily average.
specDecoder.watchFor: Hisense states 38 F, and others state nothing.

specDecoder.meaning: How high a built-in pump pushes water. It replaces gravity when the drain is high.
A tier above Energy Star that picks the most efficient models each year. It means lower power draw per liter.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Levoit lists the 2025 Most Efficient mark in this group.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which test each pint figure refers to. The Levoit separates DOE from maximum and the hOmeLabs names its 80 F basis, while others only say up to. Listings that hide the basis were scored lower than those that disclose it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drain flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted drain routes and pump options. The Levoit offers four routes, while the Hisense and Whirlpool rely on the bucket or a gravity hose.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cold and damp behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for stated low-temperature limits and defrost behavior. The Hisense is the only pick with a stated 38 F limit, based on the spec sheet. Cool-room claims without a number were treated as unverified.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked Energy Star claims and brand history. The LG, GE and Whirlpool brands give a service path that marketplace names lack.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared apps, humidistats and fan logic. GE's Smart Dry and the LG app are the standouts, and we evaluated each against owner feedback patterns.

rows: Attic or garage in mild months

cards.label: Pump
cards.text: The Levoit's pump lifts water up to 3 m and suits a high drain or a sump in another room. It adds a part that needs occasional cleaning.

cards.label: Gravity
cards.text: The GE, Hisense and Whirlpool use a hose that runs downhill to a floor drain. It is simpler and cheaper but only works with a lower drain.

howToChoose.note: Choose the Levoit if the drain is above the unit, otherwise a gravity unit is simpler. Either way, mount the hose with a clip so it cannot slip out of the drain.

rows: Wi-Fi app on a compact body

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A stated low-temperature limit and auto defrost. Expect output to fall once the room drops below the mid 60s F.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Hisense lists 38 F operation, and the Levoit adds efficient running that keeps costs down. For a very cold space, step up to a larger unit.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need a pump, an app or an efficiency label. The Levoit and LG are the two to look at. Also consider whether a second smaller unit in a far corner would work better than one large machine.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The room is mild and the drain is at floor level. A Hisense or Whirlpool covers it.

maintenance.why: Lint blocks airflow and raises compressor load. Dry it fully before refitting. A second spare filter, where the maker sells one, lets you swap while the first dries.
Debris and slime clog pumps and hoses. The Levoit's pump is removable for this reason. Run a little white vinegar solution through the hose if it smells musty.
Standing water grows slime and smells.
Dust lowers heat exchange. Unplug and use a soft brush. Check the fins for bent edges and straighten them gently with a fin comb.
Built-in sensors drift. A separate reading confirms your target.

faq.q: Is 25 pints enough for a basement?
faq.a: It suits a finished basement or a mildly damp one up to roughly 1,500 sq ft. Wet walls or standing water need a bigger machine. Judge by dampness before square footage. A hygrometer reading above 60 percent after a day of running means the unit is undersized for the space.

Yes if the drain sits above the unit or the floor drain is far away. The Levoit lifts water up to 3 m. Otherwise a gravity hose is simpler. A pump also costs a little more electricity and makes a faint noise when it cycles.

No. It only adds remote control and alerts. The LG sends maintenance alerts, which is helpful for a basement you rarely enter. Manufacturers have shifted apps and shut some down, so favor a company with a long record.

faq.q: Why does my 25 pint unit collect less?
faq.a: Cool rooms and lower humidity cut output. A label taken at 95 F and 90 percent is far above what a basement delivers. Expect less in a cold space. Defrost cycles in a cool room also pause the compressor, which lowers the daily average further.

It is worth having for a machine that runs for hours. The Levoit's Most Efficient mark is the top tier. Check the EPA list to confirm. The label also helps you qualify for utility rebates in some areas.

Several years with filter care, and the compressor is the part that fails. Units that run in dusty, hot spaces wear faster. A brand with service support helps. Keep the receipt and the warranty card, since coverage often runs one to two years.
